1) Irritant/toxic ocular surface inflammation (chemical conjunctivitis / superficial keratitis)
- Most likely given recent inhalational exposure to polyurethane fumes and bilateral symptoms. Can cause subjective blurring from tear-film disruption or superficial epithelial irritation even with normal high-contrast visual acuity.

2) Tear-film instability / evaporative dry eye triggered by the irritant exposure
- Common after airborne irritants; causes fluctuating or sustained blurring that often tests as normal acuity between blinks.

3) Transient accommodative or binocular dysfunction (spasm or fatigue)
- Can produce bilateral blurred vision, especially subjectively worse for reading; may follow stress/irritation and produce normal objective acuity at distance.

4) Migraine visual phenomenon (visual aura without headache)
- Can produce transient bilateral visual disturbance; less likely given persistence for 2 days but still possible.

5) Functional (non‑organic) visual disturbance / somatic perception
- Consider if objective testing remains normal and no ocular or neurologic signs, particularly when symptoms are inconsistent.

Immediate recommendations (urgent if any occur)
- If you develop worsening vision, new eye pain, marked redness, photophobia, double vision, pupil asymmetry, or any neurologic symptoms (weakness, numbness, difficulty speaking), go to the emergency department or ophthalmology urgently.
- For now: irrigate eyes with clean water or saline if you notice ongoing irritation; stop further exposure to the product and go to fresh air; use preservative-free artificial tears for symptomatic relief.

Recommended next ophthalmic evaluation (arrange promptly with eye clinic)
- Formal monocular visual acuity with pinhole and habitual correction
- Slit‑lamp exam with fluorescein staining (look for corneal epithelial defects)
- External exam for conjunctival injection/tearing
- Color vision testing and pupil exam for afferent defect
- Intraocular pressure and dilated fundus exam if indicated
- Consider visual field testing or neuro-ophthalmology referral only if objective deficits are found
